{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.6,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R47"],
      "pins": ["R47.1", "R47.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R47 is valued \"24k\" in the component value field, but its description, MPN and footprint identify a 24 ohm part: description \"125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805\", MPN \"FRC0805J240TSD\" (the \"240\" code means 24 Ω). The value field disagrees with the part's own metadata by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "R47 should be 24 Ω, consistent with its description and MPN, or the description and MPN should be corrected if 24 kΩ was truly intended. Either way the value, part and description must agree.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R47\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "R47 sits across VOUTN and VOUTP, which carry the PoE-derived rail with C50 47uF and C16. If the part is 24 Ω, it loads that rail heavily and dissipates far more power than a 24 kΩ bleed or divider would. If the value is 24 kΩ, the part is wrong for the 0805 24 Ω stock it was specified from. Either way the BOM and schematic disagree.",
      "confidence": 0.6
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D6", "D20", "D30"],
      "pins": ["D6.2", "D20.2", "D30.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0033"],
      "observed": "The anodes of three LEDs (D6 yellow, D20 green, D30 green) are all on /NET0033, and no other pin is on that net. The anode net is not connected to +3V3, +5V or any other supply. The cathodes are driven by current-limit resistors from the CM4 status outputs (R46 from nLED2, R4 from PI_nLED_Activity, R41 from nLED3).",
      "expected": "Status LED anodes should be tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other LED anodes on this board are (for example D47 anode on +3V3, D9/D15 via R88/R85 on +3V3). Without this connection the LEDs cannot light.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"12\") (name \"/NET0033\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D20\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D6\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R46\") (pin \"2\") ... ) with R46 pin 1 on Net-(D6-K) and D6 pin 1 K on Net-(D6-K)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet activity/link and Pi activity indicator LEDs (D6, D20, D30) have no supply path, so they will never illuminate, and the status indication they are meant to provide is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R94", "R101"],
      "pins": ["R94.1", "R94.2", "R101.1", "R101.2"],
      "nets": ["NET0035", "+12V", "GND"],
      "observed": "The TPS61040 boost feedback divider is R101 = 1.8M (top, from +12V to NET0035) and R94 = 205k (bottom, NET0035 to GND). U30 FB sits on NET0035. With the TPS61040 feedback reference of about 0.2 V, this divider sets the output at roughly 0.2 × (1 + 1.8M/205k) ≈ 1.96 V, not 12 V.",
      "expected": "For a +12 V output with a 0.2 V feedback reference, the top/bottom ratio should be about 59:1 (for example 1.8 MΩ with roughly 30 kΩ on the bottom).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R94\") (value \"205k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R101\") (value \"1.8M\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U30\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"FB\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the divider is as drawn, the boost converter regulates its FB node to about 2 V and the +12 V rail is never produced, which would starve the 12 V connectors and anything on +12V.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is the R47 value field reading \"24k\" when its description and MPN say 24 Ω, a clear metadata/value mismatch. The three status-LED anodes on /NET0033 also have no connection to any supply, which would leave those indicators dead. The boost feedback divider looks inconsistent with a 12 V output, but this is lower confidence."
}

anomalies.observed: R47 is valued "24k" in the component value field, but its description, MPN and footprint identify a 24 ohm part: description "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805", MPN "FRC0805J240TSD" (the "240" code means 24 Ω). The value field disagrees with the part's own metadata by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: R47 should be 24 Ω, consistent with its description and MPN, or the description and MPN should be corrected if 24 kΩ was truly intended. Either way the value, part and description must agree.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: R47 sits across VOUTN and VOUTP, which carry the PoE-derived rail with C50 47uF and C16. If the part is 24 Ω, it loads that rail heavily and dissipates far more power than a 24 kΩ bleed or divider would. If the value is 24 kΩ, the part is wrong for the 0805 24 Ω stock it was specified from. Either way the BOM and schematic disagree.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three LEDs (D6 yellow, D20 green, D30 green) are all on /NET0033, and no other pin is on that net. The anode net is not connected to +3V3, +5V or any other supply. The cathodes are driven by current-limit resistors from the CM4 status outputs (R46 from nLED2, R4 from PI_nLED_Activity, R41 from nLED3).
anomalies.expected: Status LED anodes should be tied to the 3.3 V rail, as the other LED anodes on this board are (for example D47 anode on +3V3, D9/D15 via R88/R85 on +3V3). Without this connection the LEDs cannot light.

evidence.quote: (node (ref "R46") (pin "2") ... ) with R46 pin 1 on Net-(D6-K) and D6 pin 1 K on Net-(D6-K)

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity/link and Pi activity indicator LEDs (D6, D20, D30) have no supply path, so they will never illuminate, and the status indication they are meant to provide is lost.

anomalies.observed: The TPS61040 boost feedback divider is R101 = 1.8M (top, from +12V to NET0035) and R94 = 205k (bottom, NET0035 to GND). U30 FB sits on NET0035. With the TPS61040 feedback reference of about 0.2 V, this divider sets the output at roughly 0.2 × (1 + 1.8M/205k) ≈ 1.96 V, not 12 V.
anomalies.expected: For a +12 V output with a 0.2 V feedback reference, the top/bottom ratio should be about 59:1 (for example 1.8 MΩ with roughly 30 kΩ on the bottom).
anomalies.impact: If the divider is as drawn, the boost converter regulates its FB node to about 2 V and the +12 V rail is never produced, which would starve the 12 V connectors and anything on +12V.
